o: Simulate the selection process: the first student is selected; each later student replaces the selection only if their rank is strictly smaller than the current best. Counting replacements is therefore just counting how many elements are strictly smaller than the running prefix minimum.
k: A replacement happens exactly when ranks[i] < min(ranks[0..i-1]).
Strictness matters: equal ranks never replace (Example 2).

a.i: Track the best (smallest) rank seen so far. Each subsequent element strictly below it triggers a replacement and updates the best. This is a single linear scan — no data structures needed.
s: For each following x: if x < best, ans++ and best = x.

w: Trivially optimal; the only mistake to avoid is using <= instead of <. Follow-up variants: count replacements if ties replace (change to <=), or if selection restarts after each replacement (same thing here since the replacement is always the new best).
